job.title: Health, Safety & Environment Manager - Agribusiness
job.description:
The Company
Our client is an established and well-regarded agribusiness group operating sites across Victoria and New South Wales. With a strong manufacturing and operational footprint, the business supplies a range of food and agricultural products to domestic and international customers and continues to invest in consistent systems, operational improvement and best-practice standards across its sites.

The Opportunity
In this role, we are seeking an experienced Health, Safety & Environment Manager to lead and coordinate the HSE function across multiple sites. This is a hands-on position, with the person responsible for developing consistent systems, policies and standards, monitoring legislative compliance, supporting operational leaders and driving continuous improvement across the Group.

You will provide specialist advice, coaching and oversight across the business, working closely with Site Managers, General Managers, HR and operational teams. Key areas of focus will include HSE management systems, incident investigation, audit coordination, contractor management, environmental compliance, return to work governance and the continued improvement of the Group Safety Management System.

About You
Ideally the successful candidate will bring:
  • 8+ years working in a similar role, which will naturally highlight your strong knowledge of Australian WHS and environmental legislation.
  • Experience developing and improving HSE management systems, policies and procedures.
  • Ability to influence, coach and support operational leaders across multiple sites using a grounded perspective rather than a head office approach.
  • Practical experience in incident investigation, corrective actions and audit coordination.
  • Exposure to contractor management, return to work programs and safety committee governance.
  • Strong communication, stakeholder management and problem-solving capability.
  • Commercially minded approach, balancing compliance requirements with practical operational outcomes
Why This Role
This is an opportunity to take ownership of a broad, group-level HSE function within an established agribusiness and food manufacturing environment. The role offers genuine influence across multiple sites, exposure to senior operational stakeholders and the ability to shape consistent safety and environmental systems across the business. For an HSE professional who enjoys balancing strategic improvement with practical, hands-on operational support, this position provides the scope to make a visible impact on safety culture, compliance and continuous improvement.

Due to the site locations, this role will require regular travel across the sites in Victoria and New South Wales, with a minimum travel expectation of a week per month on the road.

For a confidential discussion or to find out more, please phone Ryan Hoiberg on 1300 380 701 or apply via www.rimfireresources.com.au

job.title: Business Development Manager - WA
job.description:
About The Client:

Our client is recognised as one of Australia’s leading precision agriculture providers. With commercial momentum gained in the east coast of Australia, and as a result of a number of key strategic relationships, the group is now experiencing an exciting phase of expansion into key markets. As part of this, the group now wishes to leverage their market position, by appointing a highly motivated client facing professional into the business as WA Business Development Manager. With the support of a highly respected and networked leadership team, rarely does such a career opportunity present.

About The Position:

Reporting to the National Commercial Manager, the Business Development Manager – WA will be primarily responsible for growing and maintaining the client base in Western Australia. As part of the execution of the national commercial plan, this will involve one-on-one, on-farm and industry interaction with growers, agronomists and retailers. Using your proven experience gained in technical agronomy, you will tailor precision agricultural solutions for each client, enabling enhanced agronomy decisions, which will deliver increased farm-system efficiencies. This role involves travel to client sites - and candidates are welcome to apply from a metropolitan or regional location in Western Australia.

About The Person:

To be successful in this position, candidates will require the following:
  • Client facing experience gained in the Australian broadacre sector (critical)
  • A relentless focus on customer experience
  • A sound technological knowledge of WA agronomy, soils and/or farming systems
  • Experience delivering high-value services
  • Excellent time management and communication/presentation skills
  • Commercial acumen and an affinity for information technology
  • High levels of career motivation
  • Relevant qualifications
On Offer:

On offer, is the opportunity to join a growing organisation, a generous salary package plus a vehicle allowance and tools of trade. The Business Development Manager will also be encouraged to participate in ongoing training, personal development and the group’s financial incentive scheme. In addition to significant scope for career advancement, this “work from home” opportunity also offers a large amount of autonomy and work-life balance.

To Apply:

For further information, please call Charles Linton on 1300 380 701. Applications via www.rimfireresources.com.au.

job.title: Senior Asset Manager (GIS)
job.description:
The Company
Our client, Murray Irrigation, is seeking a Senior Asset Officer (GIS) to lead the management, data integrity, and continuous improvement of the organisation’s Asset Management System (AMS) and Geographic Information System (GIS). This role drives best-practice spatial data governance, provides expert technical guidance, and delivers strategic analysis to underpin asset lifecycle decision-making across the organisation.
Murray Irrigation is the largest private irrigation water delivery company in Australia, formed as an unlisted public company in March 1995 when the NSW Government privatised its Murray Irrigation area and districts. The company's irrigators are also shareholders and include 2,100 landholdings across 724,000 hectares in the Southern Riverina. 
The Opportunity
Reporting to the Strategic Asset Manager, this role offers flexible working arrangements (onsite, remote, or hybrid, with a minimum requirement of 3 days per month on site). The role acts as the technical authority on GIS and asset data matters, with key responsibilities including:
  • Leading the ongoing management, enhancement, and governance of AMS and GIS systems to ensure high availability, data quality, and access control.
  • Leading the GIS workstream for new Asset Management System implementations, including designing, building, and maintaining integrations between GIS platforms and enterprise systems.
  • Designing, building, and maintaining a suite of high-quality web maps, dashboards, and field collection applications (ArcGIS Online, ArcGIS Pro, Field Maps, Survey123) to drive capability across field and operational teams.
  • Automating spatial data workflows, ETL processes, and repetitive tasks using scripting tools such as Python, Arcade, FME, or equivalent.
  • Conducting advanced spatial analysis, geographic modelling, and scenario analysis to support capital planning, asset replacement schedules, and resource allocation.
  • Leading data quality improvement programs, establishing QA/QC processes, and governing spatial data collection standards for field operations.
  • Providing technical guidance, training, and support across business units to build organisational capability in spatial systems and asset data tools.
About You
The ideal candidate will be a forward-thinking spatial specialist with strong technical expertise in enterprise GIS platforms, spatial data governance, and system integrations. To be successful in this role, you will have the following experience and attributes:
  • Tertiary qualifications in GIS, Spatial Science, Surveying, or a related field combined with substantial experience in a senior or specialist enterprise GIS role.
  • Extensive experience in the administration, architecture, and strategic customisation of the full ESRI product suite (ArcGIS Online, ArcGIS Pro, ESRI Web Apps, Field Maps, Survey123).
  • Demonstrated experience with enterprise data management systems, system administration, configuration, and GIS–enterprise system integrations.
  • Scripting proficiency in Python, Arcade, FME, or equivalent to automate spatial workflows and data pipelines.
  • Demonstrated expertise in designing, managing, and improving field data collection apps and user workflows for non-technical stakeholders.
  • Highly developed written and verbal communication skills, with a proven ability to translate complex technical concepts for senior leadership and operational teams.
  • Strong project leadership skills, with the ability to work autonomously, exercise sound professional judgment, and drive continuous improvement.
Why This Role
Unique opportunity to drive spatial innovation and lead the enterprise GIS function for a major regional water infrastructure provider. To enquire about this role, please phone Charles MacCallum on 1300 380 701 for a confidential conversation. Or apply online with a tailored cover letter and resume.

job.title: Business Manager- Field Crop Research
job.description:
The Company
Our client is a leader in providing science based, agricultural field research services, conducting trials in the major broadacre and horticultural cropping regions of Australia. With offices and staff strategically positioned, providing a full suite of services, they are focussed on helping advance new technologies to market and developing new agricultural inputs and systems.

With experienced staff and working with leading edge technology, business is based on delivering results and creating great relationships with clients, so they are committed to open and consistent communication.

The research work is comprehensive and diverse covering a wide range of broadacre and horticultural trees & crops across residue, efficacy and breeding trials. 

The role
A vacancy now exists for a Business Manager to manage the northern research unit across Northern NSW and Qld. This diverse role fundamentally supports your regional managers and drives business.

Reporting to the National Business Manager, you will be responsible for:
  • Developing and leading teams
  • High quality trial execution
  • Maintaining strong client relationships
  • Achieving commercial targets
  • Ensuring compliance with company policy and safety standards
This involves working closely with your team of two Regional Managers and associated regionally based operations / logistics staff.

Being a management role, there is limited time in field and travelling.

The Person
The successful person will have the following skills and attributes:
  • Leadership experience (build, manage high performing teams)
  • Excellent communications and stakeholder engagement skills
  • Significant experience managing R&D field trials across diverse crops and environments
  • Ability to manage logistics (people, equipment, operations)
  • Strong commercial acumen (budgeting, quoting, revenue generation)
  • Relevant tertiary qualifications in Agriculture/ Business /Commerce
You will likely have an established professional reputation with strong networks across industry, private and public sectors.

A generous salary package including vehicle is on offer for the successful candidate. Toowoomba or Brisbane are ideal locations for this role, so would suit candidates with growing families requiring education, cultural or sporting facilities.

You may have field trial work experience with crop protection or seed suppliers, rural retail distribution, university or government department research or Research Development Corporations (RDC’s) and now looking for a new challenge, to step up into a leadership role.

Come and join a leading research agribusiness, bringing your style of people leadership and business management skills. The skilled and dynamic team is growing, accumulating a wealth of experience, providing growth and learning opportunities around the country.

Please call Al Kellaway on 1300 380 701 for a discussion and copy of the Position Description, or apply via www.rimfireresources.com.au

job.title: Trading Accountant - Agribusiness
job.description:
The Company

CHS Broadbent is a leading Australian agribusiness supply chain company with grain marketing, storage, logistics and export operations on the east coast of Australia. CHS Broadbent own and operate grain storage, container packing, and grain freight operations through Queensland, New South Wales, and Victoria. They are widely recognised by grain producers and markets as leaders in providing reliable, dependable, customer focused service.

The Opportunity

As part of their continued growth, CHS Broadbent are looking for a Trading Accountant to join their Finance team. This role will support the financial control, accounting, reporting and analysis of CHS Broadbent’s grain trading activities, providing independent oversight across commodity positions, grain inventories, mark-to-market valuations, profit and loss reporting, hedging activities and trading exposures.

Working closely with the Trading, Risk, Logistics, Operations and Finance teams, you will support commercial decision-making while ensuring compliance with accounting standards, internal controls and risk management frameworks. The role will be involved in weekly and monthly grain and trading P&L reporting, inventory reconciliations, commodity valuations, management reporting, budgeting, forecasting and process improvement initiatives including integration of AI tools and identifying new opportunities and solutions previously not explored.

About You

To be successful in this position you will have:
  • A degree in Accounting, Finance or Commerce, with CPA or CA qualification.
  • Experience in commercial accounting, management accounting, commodity accounting or a related finance role.
  • Strong understanding of inventory reconciliation, financial reporting, P&L analysis and management accounting.
  • Exposure to grain, commodity trading, logistics or agribusiness operations would be highly regarded.
  • Strong analytical capability, attention to detail and confidence working with large volumes of financial and operational data.
  • Advanced Excel skills, with experience using ERP systems, commodity trading platforms, Power Query, Power BI or similar reporting tools beneficial.
  • The ability to partner effectively with trading, operations, logistics, risk and finance stakeholders.
Why This Role

In return, you will be joining an expanding agribusiness with multiple domestic assets and a growing export operation, in a role that provides broad exposure across trading, finance, risk and operations.

If you wish to confidentially discuss this role, please give Ryan Hoiberg or Charlie MacCallum a call on 1300 380 701 or apply now at www.rimfireresources.com.au.

job.title: Head of Commercial Operations
job.description:
The Company:

Consolidated Pastoral Company (CPC) is a leading Australian managed, UK owned Agribusiness with strong ESG values. CPC owns and operates a portfolio of 11 station aggregations in Australia and 2 feedlots in Indonesia. 

Across more than 5.5m hectares of land, the CPC team care for more than 400,000 head of cattle, 100,000 sheep, 50,000 goats and produce a diverse range of crops. With an asset base in excess of AUD$1.5 billion, CPC supplies a variety of domestic and international customers. CPC is developing new business streams in emissions reduction and sequestration, biodiversity and sustainable energy production.  

The welfare of their people and animals is of paramount importance to CPC and the CPC WHS and HR team partners with all members of CPC to foster a positive safety culture and performance.

The Opportunity:

CPC is well down the path and is committed to transforming CPC from a leading cattle business into a globally significant agribusiness with a strong presence in cattle, sheep, goats, crops and natural capital whilst developing sustainable energy opportunities. They will continue to undergo significant growth and business diversification, and the operations team is building a deeper team for growth, succession and key person risk.

With new business streams, a more diverse geographic footprint, increased business operating environment complexity and more focus on performance and productivity, CPC requires a Head of Commercial Operations to provide further depth to the executive team as well as provide potential future succession options.  

The specific role and tasks may be adapted for the successful candidate to broaden their skills and experience rather than purely focus on their existing skills and experience.

The Person:

We are keen to hear from you If you possess the following experience, key skills and attributes:
  • Proven senior level leadership experience, ideally with exposure to livestock and/or other segments of Australian agriculture
  • High level written and verbal communications skills, projecting a professional image when representing CPC
  • Well-developed short- & long-term planning and organisational skills
  • Sound financial literacy with the ability to interrogate and interpret financial statements and provide sound strategic insight
  • High level attention to detail with a willingness to be adaptable, take on new concepts and learn
  • Ability to work as a member of geographically remote teams
  • Curious by nature, showing initiative with well-developed listening skills
  • Computer literate with tertiary qualifications in agriculture, finance, business or similar
  • Current first aid certificate and motor vehicle licence (C Class, manual)
Operational experience in livestock and/or cropping will be seen as highly advantageous as will any exposure to livestock marketing and supply chain analysis in Australian agriculture. 

Why this Role?

Rarely does a newly created senior leadership opportunity become available that plays an integral role in the transformation of a leading cattle business to a globally significant agribusiness.

If you are seeking a position with high impact, excellent future career prospects and an opportunity to make a real difference, then contact Mick Hay on 1300 380 701 for a confidential discussion. Applications via www.rimfireresources.com.au

job.title: Manager, Commercialisation
job.description:
The Company

Grains Research and Development Corporation (GRDC) is responsible for planning, investing, and overseeing research, development, and extension for the grains sector in Australia. They meet the evolving needs of grain growers with a vision to be regarded as the grower’s “RD&E department.” GRDC believes it should be a valued grower asset that is open, transparent, and trusted - a true research partner who seeks to be agile and business like in their operations and improve productivity and profitability for growers.

The Opportunity

GRDC is seeking a Manager, Commercialisation who will support GRDC’s purpose by structuring, delivering and actively managing commercial pathways for GRDC’s investment outputs, including scoping and negotiating translational agreements from material transfer agreements to complex multi-party licences. This key role contributes to short, medium and long-term strategies for the commercialisation, utilisation and impact of GRDC investment outputs, including active portfolio management of IP and technology assets, through leveraging internal, national and international capability.
You will be working with the greater organisation right from the early stages of identification, development and planning of potential opportunities right through to realisation, including ongoing post-investment management of commercial agreements, IP assets and performance against commercialisation objectives. You will initiate and deliver ongoing management of contractual commitments, with a focus on commercial performance, utilisation and impact of GRDC-funded outputs, including IP and technology pipeline management, contract governance and compliance. Canberra location is preferred however, other offices (Adelaide, Toowoomba, Perth) may be considered for the right candidate.

This involves:
  • Supporting the organisation in scoping, structuring and establishing complex R&D investment arrangements, including multi-party collaborations and non-standard commercial frameworks
  • Leading end-to-end commercialisation and active management of GRDC IP and investment outputs
  • Managing a portfolio of GRDC’s commercialisation assets (IP, licences, data and technologies) to maximise utilisation, adoption and impact
  • Identifying, structuring and executing pathways to market, and oversee their ongoing performance and optimisation
  • Playing a central role to analysis and synthesise current and historical commercialisation data to inform commercialisation strategy, portfolio performance and investment decisions
  • Negotiating and implementing commercial arrangements that enable delivery, adoption and long-term utilisation of project outputs
  • Managing IP assets such as trademarks, breeder rights and patents, to maximise value, utilisation and industry impact
  • Monitoring and report on commercialisation performance, including adoption, revenue, and impact metrics across the portfolio
  • Identifying and contributing to process improvement
  
About You

To be successful in this influential role, you will ideally possess:
  • Experience in the agricultural or complimentary sectors that can cross multiple areas of the grains innovation ecosystem (e.g. technology, data, software)
  • Awareness of Australia’s RD&E will be seen as highly desirable
  • Demonstrated experience in commercialisation of research and innovation, including ongoing management of commercial agreements, IP and technology assets
  • An understanding of IP management and or IP and company law
  • Exceptional negotiation and influencing skills with a depth of interpersonal and problem-solving skills
  • Experience developing marketing and/or business plans and testing assumptions in market
  • A flexible attitude and approach
  • Strong analytical and strategic planning capability complimented with sound financial and business knowledge
  • Effective skills and experience to work across many different stakeholders in co-design of investments
  • Tertiary qualifications (Bachelor level or equivalent) in Agriculture or other complimentary scientific discipline, and Business, Law, Commerce or a related field
Importantly, GRDC is looking for an individual who has a service mentality to work proactively with internal and external stakeholders to ensure GRDC investments translate into tangible industry outcomes through effective commercialisation and asset management. You will be naturally resilient and proactive in nature and very much a relationship builder to listen to a broad range of views, driving consensus and action, but well positioned to influence and engage a diverse group of stakeholders.
This is a rare and exciting opportunity to make a valuable contribution to the future profitability of Australia’s grain industry. GRDC aim to enhance productivity, profitability and sustainability of Australian grain growers and benefit the industry and wider community.
For confidential enquiries and a copy of the position description, please phone Charles Linton on 1300 380 701 or apply via rimfireresources.com.au.

job.title: Product Support Representative
job.description:
The Company
Our client, MacDon is a leading global innovator in advanced harvesting technology and equipment, dedicated to enhancing agricultural productivity. MacDon work with dealers and OEMs to design, develop, manufacture, sell and support products across the world, with a worldwide reputation for excellence. They have a strong priority to build relationships that drive growth in products and distribution and work with dealer customers across Australia to connect with their farming customers.

The Position
Reporting to the Product Support Supervisor and working as part of a national team, you will act as the primary point of contact for dealer personnel to address product issues or customer concerns for the MacDon business. You will cover a pool of dealers Western Australia, with a true split north and south of Perth.  

You will:
  • Lead in territory investigation and troubleshooting, assisting with resolving any problems, and reporting them through to head office.
  • Develop and maintain relationships with Dealer support personnel to ensure a positive experience and direct point of contact to discuss any equipment.
  • Provide technical training for dealer technicians and end users
  • Perform demonstrations of new products
The Person
The ideal candidate will have:
  • Experience working with relevant agricultural equipment and its operations
  • Experience with grain harvesting equipment would be highly beneficial
  • A technical background in diagnosis and report of Mechanical, Hydraulic and Electrical systems.
  • Excellent communications skills, both written and verbal with an ability to work closely with remote teams.
  • Comfortable with regular travel in a role, with expectation of around 50-60% of this role being on the road.
  • Experience working within a relevant dealer, or speaking with dealer technicians would be beneficial.
This is an opportunity to join a business with an exceptional reputation and high quality machinery, and work with a true leader in the industry. The ideal candidate would be in Perth metro, with ability to access dealers north and south.

To confidentially discuss this opportunity, please call Ryan Hoiberg on 1300 380 701 or apply now via www.rimfireresources.com.au

job.title: Head of Operations - Horticulture
job.description:
The Company

Impact Ag Australia is on a mission to accelerate agriculture that activates the power of nature.

They partner with clients to deliver high-performing agricultural assets that integrate regenerative practices, commercial discipline, and long-term environmental value. Their team works at the intersection of agriculture, investment, and natural capital, creating practical solutions that improve asset performance while supporting enduring ecological outcomes.

The Opportunity

The Head of Operations – Horticulture is a senior leadership role responsible for delivering the operational plans for all existing and future horticultural assets under management. In addition, the role will provide support to two existing broadacre assets, located in Southern Queensland and Central New South Wales.

The role is responsible for executing approved operational plans and contributing to the delivery of investor approved investment plans, through strong on farm leadership, operational excellence, and disciplined execution.

The role provides direct leadership to on-farm teams, ensures operational excellence, and drives alignment with the investor-approved strategic business plan. This position holds accountability for performance, compliance, culture, and continuous improvement across all assigned assets.

About You

This is a senior-level corporate leadership position, and we are keen to speak with candidates who can demonstrate the following skills, experience and key competencies:
  • Minimum 10 years’ experience in farm management with a focus on intensive irrigated horticultural production, ideally with a strong exposure to broadacre production and financial management
  • Strong exposure to working with drip or sprinkler irrigation systems within permanent crops as well as the marketing of horticultural commodities and managing on farm processing of horticultural commodities
  • Demonstrated understanding of regenerative agriculture, WHS, WorkCover requirements, environmental obligations, and animal welfare legislation
  • Proven experience developing and implementing budgets, operational plans, and performance systems with exposure to project management highly regarded
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office and farm management software (Agworld or equivalent)
  • Tertiary qualifications in agriculture, agronomy, horticulture, or related field as well as a current Australian Driver’s Licence
Ability to lead and manage diverse teams and contractors through clear communication and example-setting.

Strong commercial acumen and operational discipline with high attention to detail and strong influencing, communication, and collaborative problem-solving skills.

Why This Role

This is an opportunity to join a business with a clear ambition: to demonstrate that agriculture can deliver strong financial performance while improving the natural systems that underpin it. Through active asset management and innovative natural capital strategies, Impact Ag Australia is helping shape the next generation of agricultural investment.

A highly competitive remuneration package is on offer for the successful candidate. To learn more or for a confidential discussion, please call Mick Hay on 1300 380 701. Applications via www.rimfireresources.com.au

job.title: Stewardship Field Officer - Victoria
job.description:
The Company

Established in 1993, Agsafe is a not-for-profit wholly owned subsidiary of CropLife Australia. Stewardship focused, Agsafe is committed to promoting the safe and responsible management of agricultural chemicals across Australia. Their mission is to support and educate the AgChem supply chain, from manufacture to end of life, to uphold the highest standards of safety and product stewardship.

Through comprehensive training programs, industry-leading certification, and recycling initiatives such as drumMUSTER, ChemClear, and bagMUSTER, they protect both people and the environment. 25 years on, drumMUSTER is a true success story, one of the nation’s leading recycling programs across all industries.

Agsafe is a future looking organisation, where the culture has evolved to be focussed on client facing service provision, rather than regulation.

The Opportunity

Agsafe is seeking a Stewardship Field Officer to provide senior field leadership to deliver their national training, accreditation, and quality assurance programs. The role champions the regional rollout of the drumMUSTER and bagMUSTER stewardship initiatives in the Victoria region. This position is central to upholding Agsafe’ s standards through assessment delivery, regional presence, and stakeholder engagement.

Key responsibilities include:
  • Client support services - premise reviews and training
  • DrumMUSTER program oversight
  • bagMUSTER rollout and expansion
  • Business development and program Innovation
  • Reporting, compliance, and administration
About You

We are keen to hear from you if you are:
  • A self-starter, who enjoys engaging stakeholders across government and commercial sectors
  • Experienced in training/education, WHS and or audits
  • Able to demonstrate ability to develop and maintain commercial relationships
  • Qualified in Cert IV in Workplace Training & Assessment or equivalent (or willingness to obtain), and/or have a Lead Auditor Certificate (or equivalent)
  • Willingness to travel across your region with regular nights away from home
  • Affinity or passion for agriculture
Why This Role

This is an exciting opportunity to work closely with the agricultural chemical industry where you can make a significant impact on Australia’s sustainability - enabling the safe collection, recycling, and disposal of agvet chemical containers, agricultural plastic bags, and unwanted or obsolete chemicals across the state.

In addition to an attractive salary package, a fully maintained vehicle, and tools of trade (laptop, iPad, and home office) will be provided.

For more information please phone David Jackson on 1300 380 701 or apply via www.rimfireresources.com.au with a current Resume and a brief Cover Letter.

job.title: Regional Sales Manager
job.description:
The Company
Riordan Fuels is a proudly Australian, family-owned fuel business supplying regional communities, agriculture and industry across regional Victoria and Southern New South Wales. With a strong bulk fuel supply offer and a growing network of 24/7 diesel self-serve sites, the business has built its reputation around reliability, service and long-standing regional relationships.

As the business continues to expand its regional footprint, Riordan Fuels is seeking a commercially astute sales leader to help drive growth, strengthen key customer partnerships and support the next phase of its sales strategy.

The Opportunity
Reporting to the General Manager - Fuels, the Regional Sales Manager will lead and develop a team of sales representatives while managing key customer relationships across the farming, transport and industrial sectors. This is a hands-on regional sales leadership role requiring a balance of people leadership, account management, new business development and commercial discipline.

The role will suit someone who enjoys being close to customers, understands the importance of reliable supply and service, and can identify opportunities to grow share across an established regional customer base.

Key responsibilities will include:
  • Lead, coach and motivate a regional sales team to achieve growth, retention and customer engagement targets.
  • Manage and grow key account relationships across agriculture, transport and industrial markets.
  • Identify and convert new business opportunities across the company’s regional footprint.
  • Work closely with operations to ensure customer commitments, supply requirements and service expectations are met.
  • Provide regular reporting on sales performance, pipeline activity, customer trends and broader market conditions.
  • Support pricing strategy, tender activity and contract negotiations for major accounts.
  • Represent Riordan Fuels at industry events and within local regional communities.
About You
To be successful in this role, you will bring proven experience in sales leadership or senior sales within fuel, agribusiness, transport or another related regional industry. You will be comfortable leading a team, building trusted customer relationships and operating with a strong commercial focus.

You will be a proactive, relationship-led operator who can work autonomously across a regional territory while staying connected to broader business priorities. Strong negotiation skills, sound computer literacy and a willingness to embrace technology and AI-enabled tools will also be important.

You will be comfortable travelling across Victoria, Southern New South Wales and South Australia as required for the role to support the ongoing growth of the business.

Why This Role
This is an opportunity to join a well-established, family-owned Australian business with a genuine connection to regional communities. An attractive salary package will be offered based on experience, including a company vehicle and staff fuel discount.

To Apply
For confidential enquiries and a copy of the Position Description, please phone Ryan Hoiberg on 1300 380 701 or apply via rimfireresources.com.au.

job.title: Transport Scheduler - Grain & Logistics
job.description:
The Company

Our client is a well-established and respected agribusiness operating across grain and logistics services. They play a critical role supporting growers and customers through efficient, compliant and reliable transport operations. With a strong focus on safety, service and continuous improvement, the business offers a supportive team environment and long-term career opportunity.

The Opportunity

Reporting to the Transport Manager, this role is central to the day-to-day coordination of transport operations. You will be responsible for scheduling and allocating trucks in line with customer requirements and National Fatigue Laws, while working closely drivers and the broader transport administration team.
This is a highly engaged, detail-driven role where no two days are the same. You will liaise closely with drivers, customers and internal stakeholders to ensure orders are planned, communicated and delivered efficiently. There is also scope to contribute to improving systems, processes and transport outcomes as the business continues to evolve.

About You

You may already be working in a transport scheduling or logistics coordination role, and ideally you would have a passion for the grain industry and/or Australian agriculture. You may even come from a broader agricultural background with a different skill set, and be ready to step into a more specialised scheduling position.

We would be open to speaking with you if you match the above, and have also:
  • Experience in transport scheduling, logistics or a similar coordination role
  • An understanding of compliance requirements, ideally including fatigue management
  • High attention to detail and strong organisational skills
  • Clear communication skills and the confidence to deal with drivers and customers daily
  • A calm, practical approach in a fast-paced operational environment
Why This Role

job.title: Technical Development Manager - Southern Region
job.description:
The Company

LongReach Plant Breeders, a joint venture between Advanta Seeds and Syngenta, is one of Australia’s leading wheat breeding and commercialisation companies. For more than a quarter of a century, the business has conducted research, developed new products and introduced technologies that ultimately improve grower profitability.

With a strong reputation in the Australian grains industry, LongReach continues to build a competitive wheat portfolio through market-led breeding, technical development and commercial partnerships. The business is focused on delivering varieties that meet grower needs, perform in Australian farming systems and support continued growth across the market.

The Opportunity

Reporting to the Commercial Manager, this role will manage LongReach’s product development and advanced line commercialisation across the Southern Region. It is a highly market-facing technical role, supporting the transfer of knowledge between the wheat breeding program, growers, agronomists, advisers and broader industry stakeholders.

The role will ensure new wheat varieties, agronomic practices and research outcomes are effectively evaluated, communicated and adopted across farming systems. Just as importantly, it will bring market, technical and grower feedback back into the breeding program to help shape pipeline and portfolio decisions.

Key areas of focus include:
  • Coordinating product development trials, demonstration sites and variety evaluation activity
  • Translating breeding and research outcomes into practical information for growers and advisers
  • Delivering field days, workshops, technical updates and industry presentations
  • Building relationships with growers, agronomists, consultants, seed companies and industry bodies
  • Supporting product advancement, variety release and commercialisation planning
  • Providing technical, market and farming system feedback to breeders and the commercial team
This position will also play an important role in LongReach’s engagement with the NVT program, grower groups, retail agronomy networks, independent agronomists and key industry events across South Australia and Victoria.

About You

We are seeking a practical, technically strong and relationship-driven grains professional who brings:
  • 5+ years’ experience in cereal agronomy, broadacre cropping or a related technical environment
  • A graduate qualification in agriculture, agronomy or a related discipline
  • Strong knowledge of Southern Region farming systems across South Australia and Victoria
  • Experience in field agronomics, cereal farming methods, disease assessment and trial evaluation
  • An understanding of plant breeding operations, genetics and selection methodologies
  • Strong communication, networking and stakeholder engagement skills
  • The ability to work independently, organise field activity and travel widely across cropping regions
Most importantly, you will be self-motivated, commercially aware and confident working with growers, advisers, researchers and internal teams to turn technical insight into practical value in the paddock.

Why This Role

This is a rare opportunity to join LongReach Plant Breeders in a role that aligns closely to the science, the market and the grower. You will have the chance to influence how new wheat varieties are evaluated, positioned, released and adopted across one of Australia’s most important grain-growing regions.

If you are a technically capable grains professional who enjoys working closely alongside  growers, advisers and industry, we would love to hear from you. For a confidential discussion, contact Ryan Hoiberg on 1300 380 701. Applications via www.rimfireresources.com.au

job.title: Independent Chair
job.description:
The Red Meat Advisory Council (RMAC) is the policy leadership and advisory forum for Australia’s 80,000 red meat and livestock businesses across the supply chain to grow trust, pride and demand in Australian red meat. RMAC is responsible for ensuring a strong, effective and collaborative working relationship between the red-meat industry and Federal Government.
​
Their member Peak Industry Bodies provide leadership, formulate policy and set strategic imperatives for the sectors they represent, and they work closely with their respective Research and Development Corporations to set research, development, extension and marketing priorities that support the prosperity of the Australian red meat and livestock sector.
  
The board of RMAC is comprised of six industry appointed directors drawn from RMAC’s members supported by a small secretariat.

Key functions include:
  • Fostering a forum for industry good between producers, lot feeders, livestock exporters and processors of beef, sheepmeat and goatmeat
  • Guide the progressive implementation of Red Meat 2030 and the formulation of its successor strategy through working with six members and industry service providers
  • A formal advisory board to the Federal Minister for Agriculture
  • Custodians of the Red Meat Memorandum of Understanding and the Red Meat Industry Fund
  • Directing the Australian Beef Sustainability Framework and the Industry Corporate Affairs Unit.
This Independent Chair is a skills-based appointment with the following key qualities:
  • Demonstrated expertise in corporate governance in Chair and Director roles with the ability to revise Board governance procedures to improve organisational accountability and transparency in line with best practice
  • Future focussed leader capable of navigating an environment of constant change and solving complex problems with both industry and government
  • Superior communications skills including the ability to persuade and build consensus at the highest level of industry, government and community
  • The ability to act as a national spokesperson on behalf of an industry as needed
  • High level of authenticity, professionalism and credibility
  • Expertise and knowledge of the Australian red meat and livestock supply chain
This is an outstanding and unique opportunity to lead the red meat and livestock sector in this critically important position across policy leadership and advisory.

For an initial discussion, please call Mick Hay on 1300 380 701. Qualified individuals from diverse range of backgrounds are encouraged to apply. Applications should include a cover letter and CV via www.rimfireresources.com.au

job.title: Head of Innovation & Business Development
job.description:
The Company:
DataGene is an independent, industry-owned organisation responsible for driving genetic gain and herd improvement in the Australian dairy industry with their key activities being research, development and extension.

DataGene performs many pre-competitive herd improvement operations, including genetic services, software development, herd testing, herd recording and data systems as well as providing software and strategy services to deliver solutions for Australian and international customers across dairy and agriculture.

The Position:

The Head of Innovation and Business Development is an exciting new opportunity, created to lead the evolution of DataGene’s genetics and breeding technologies and farm data services strategy, with a strong focus on growth, industry value, and business impact.

The role leads DataGene’s customer-facing innovation, business development, and industry adoption activities, and is accountable for translating industry needs, partnership opportunities and emerging ideas into commercially and strategically viable products and services that deliver value to Australian dairy farm businesses.

A key part of the role is to build strong relationships across member organisations, dairy producers, intermediary partners, and industry stakeholders to drive measurable uptake and impact of DataGene products and services on-farm, and to contribute to farm profitability and broader industry sustainability and competitiveness.

A core responsibility is to assess strategic and commercial opportunities, and to develop and execute a clear business development strategy that leverages intermediary networks — including member organisations, veterinarians, farm consultants, and industry advisors — to drive adoption at scale.

The Person:

To be successful in this demanding but highly rewarding role, you will possess the following key skills and background:

Essential:
  • Demonstrated experience in business development including identifying and progressing growth opportunities, partnerships and/or new product offerings through indirect channels
  • Strong commercial acumen and proven experience developing business cases and assessing strategic fit, value and feasibility of new opportunities
  • Demonstrated leadership experience with the ability to build and develop capability in others
  • Demonstrated ability to build credibility and influence with senior external stakeholders and represent an organisation effectively in industry settings
  • Experience in developing, delivering or selling data-driven or technology-enabled products and services
  • Experience translating customer and market insight into product requirements and priorities
  • Strong understanding of how to drive adoption, customer value and measurable uptake beyond stakeholder engagement alone
  • Ability to operate at both strategic and operational levels in a player-coach capacity
Highly Desirable:
  • Strong knowledge of the dairy value chain (producer through to processor and retail)
  • Established dairy industry relationships
  • Experience working with veterinarians, consultants, advisors or agricultural intermediaries
  • Experience building or leading product management functions
This is an outstanding newly created opportunity to play a key role in assisting in the evolution of DataGene’s genetics and breeding technologies and farm data strategy.

If you have a genuine passion for business development, ideally with exposure to the Australian Dairy, then in the first instance, please call Mick Hay on 1300 380 701 for an initial discussion or further information. Applications via www.rimfireresources.com.au

job.title: Lead Production Agronomist
job.description:
The Company
GenTech Seeds is a recognised premium brand in Australian agribusiness and the exclusive producer and distributor of Pioneer® brand products in Australia.

The business works closely with growers to produce hybrid seed products suited to Australian farming systems, with a major seed manufacturing and distribution site based at Narromine in Central West NSW. The Narromine site brings together production, quality, field operations and distribution within a highly seasonal seed production environment.

The Opportunity
Reporting to the Site Manager, this role will lead technical agronomy across commercial seed production in the Macquarie Valley.

The role is focused on corn through summer and canola through winter, with some involvement in sorghum, production trials and broader improvement projects. It combines crop agronomy, grower engagement and close collaboration with production, field and quality teams.

Key responsibilities include:
  • Manage seasonal agronomy programs across corn, canola and sorghum seed production.
  • Support growers with crop establishment, nutrition, irrigation, pest and disease decisions.
  • Monitor crop performance, seasonal risk, yield potential and seed quality requirements.
  • Contribute to production planning, trials and continuous improvement projects.
Seed production experience would be valuable, but the business is open to experienced agronomists from broader broadacre, row crop or production backgrounds who can bring technical depth, sound judgement and the right team approach.

About You
You are a practical agronomist who enjoys being close to the crop, the grower and the commercial outcome.

Experience in corn, canola or seed production would be valuable, although sound crop agronomy, good judgement and grower communication will be the key.

You will bring:
  • Agronomy experience across broadacre, irrigated or seed production systems.
  • Confidence working directly with growers, contractors and operational teams.
  • Sound judgement across crop performance, timing, quality and seasonal risk.
  • A hands-on, accountable approach with the ability to take ownership of a region.
Why This Role?
This is a genuine opportunity to step into a senior agronomy role with clear ownership of a key production region. You will be close to the decisions that affect crop performance, seed quality and grower outcomes, while working within a respected national business with strong systems, established grower relationships and a premium brand in the market.

For someone who enjoys technical agronomy, commercial production and building trust with growers, this role offers the chance to have real influence across a high-value seed production program.

How to Apply
For a confidential discussion, contact Marcela Rocha Lima on 1300 380 701. Applications via www.rimfireresources.com.au.

job.title: Program Director, Plant Biosecurity Research Initiative
job.description:
The Company

Hort Innovation Australia (HIA) is an organisation that strives for better results for horticultural growers and those across the horticulture supply chain. It is the grower owned, not for profit Research and Development Corporation (RDC) for Australia’s horticultural sector. 

HIA invest substantially into research and development, marketing, adoption, data and international trade initiatives to improve the profitability, productivity and global competitiveness of the 37-levy paying Australian horticultural industries. Investment decisions are prioritised by current needs in each horticulture industry in consultation with growers.
  
The Opportunity

Under the values of and coordinated by HIA, the Program Director, Plant Biosecurity Research Initiative is a pivotal and influential role working with and representing seven RDC’s coordinating plant biosecurity research. The RDC’s are AgriFutures Australia, Cotton Research and Development Corporation, Forest and Wood Products Australia Limited, Grains Research and Development Corporation, Horticulture Innovation Australia Limited, Sugar Research Australia (SRA) Limited, Wine Australia.
  
You will take responsibility for delivering the Plant Biosecurity Research Institute program (PBRI) and will champion the research collaboration of PBRI members, with a specific focus is plant biosecurity research. The PBRI was established in 2017 following the Intergovernmental Agreement on Biosecurity Review, which identified poor coordination of biosecurity research and innovation, particularly across sectors. Since then, it has recognised biosecurity gaps (and continues to do so) resulting in $132m in funding dedicated to cross-RDC research projects.
  
The programs overall success hinges on the Project Director, while specific programs are run and executed within the RDC’s.  
  
The role involves:
  • Leading and responsibility for collaboration, stakeholder management, influencing outcomes and program deliverables
  • Identify and address R&D gaps in plant biosecurity
  • Lead the PBRI Strategy
  • Foster cross sectoral priorities and collaboration
  • Maintain governance and success of the programs that are operated by the seven RDC’s
  • Convene and facilitate PBRI meetings to ensure program is aligning with outcome expectations and report accordingly
About You

To be successful in this role you will have:
  • Exceptional stakeholder management skills, including the ability to influence without authority, and an ability to build and manage strategic collaborations
  • Have dealt with science-based stakeholders across agriculture and many levels of government including DAFF who also partner the program
  • Understand Australia’s plant biosecurity system and the national frameworks that support it.
  • Experience to distil and decipher complex data and programs into high level briefings and reports, with an ability to communicate and present complex scientific issues clearly
  • Lead stakeholder engagement and communications including media content
  • Have a project or program management background
  • Ability and experience to maintain a helicopter view of the program, but monitor and report on various projects against expectations
  • Relevant Tertiary qualifications
Why This Role  

This is an exceptional opportunity to leverage your collaboration and influencing skills across a broad range of stakeholders and delivering meaningful outcomes in the biosecurity of plants.
  
For confidential enquiries and a copy of the Position Description, please phone David Jackson or Mick Hay on 1300 380 701 or apply via rimfireresources.com.au .

job.title: Project Officer - Biosecurity
job.description:
The Company
Australian Eggs is a member-owned, not-for-profit organisation delivering marketing and RD&E services for the Australian egg industry. Guided by the vision, Be Part of Something Good, it invests in industry sustainability, productivity, resilience, animal health, food safety and biosecurity.

The Australian poultry industries face increasing risks from emergency animal diseases and other biosecurity threats. To support industry preparedness and response capability, Australian Eggs is seeking a Biosecurity Project Officer to join its growing Risk Program team.
 
The Opportunity
Reporting to the Manager - EAD Preparedness, the Biosecurity Project Officer will support projects and extension to industry to strengthen biosecurity and emergency animal disease preparedness across the Australian egg industry.

Combining project management, stakeholder engagement and technical coordination, key responsibilities include:
  • Managing biosecurity and food safety projects within the Risk Program
  • Supporting RD&E activities focused on preparedness and resilience
  • Project management, coordinating timelines, reporting, deliverables and stakeholder communication
  • Preparing reports and presentations for industry, government and technical audiences
  • Collaborating with farmers, veterinarians, researchers, consultants and government agencies
  • Representing Australian Eggs in EAD preparedness and response activities
About You
The successful candidate will bring:
  • Strong project management across multiple priorities, stakeholders and deadlines
  • Experience in biosecurity, animal health, livestock, or a related field. Poultry will be a noted advantage.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement skills across industry and government
  • Experience supporting research, innovation or extension projects
  • Excellent written communication and reporting skills
  • Relevant tertiary qualifications or significant related experience
You will be proactive, flexible, organised and able to balance technical detail with practical project delivery across diverse stakeholder groups.

Why This Role
This is a unique opportunity to work at the centre of Australia’s egg industry on projects supporting farm resilience, EAD preparedness and national biosecurity outcomes, including H5 bird flu. Australian Eggs has a collaborative and positive team culture, supporting one of Australia’s important agricultural sectors.

To Apply
For a confidential discussion, please contact Mark Turner or David Jackson on 1300 380 701 or apply online through Rimfire Resources.

job.title: General Manager - Faulkner Farming
job.description:
The Company

Gunn Agri Partners was established in 2013 and provides agricultural investment and farm management services for Australian, North American and European investors. They adopt an industry-leading framework that integrates sustainability in the design and delivery of their strategies and a mandate to transparently report against investor’s target outcomes.

Focusing on mixed farming enterprises and natural asset development, they manage a ~$1.05B portfolio of investment assets across various platforms. By lifting productivity and optimising land use, they integrate a sustainable enterprise mix of cropping, grazing and biodiversity conservation.

This portfolio, Faulkner Farming, also known as the Transforming Farming Platform, established in 2021, consists of four aggregations spread across NSW and South Australia, comprising 21kha. They are well resourced to meet targets, and operate in a fluid and quick decision environment, empowering the GM with clear delegation. Modern machinery utilising the latest hi tech, ensures a reliable fleet.

The Opportunity

The position of General Manager – Faulkner Farming, will lead the team with responsibility for overall performance of the business reporting to the Managing Directors and the Faulkner Farming Board.

The role will be responsible for all aspects of business and farm performance including operations productivity, profitability and sustainability, financial management and reporting, statutory requirements, compliance and control, external liaison and process improvement.

You will be a role model in the core values of the business – including integrity, teamwork and community commitment. A comprehensive back office provides support for the General Manager and the Faulkner Farming business.

Specifically, this involves:
  • leading and managing farm aggregation managers and their teams
  • driving workplace health and safety and building a robust safety culture
  • setting and managing budgets and forecasts,
  • managing natural capital assets,
  • implementing the sustainability policy of the businesses,
  • oversee all capital expenditure programs, including the implementation of sustainability strategies.
About You

To be successful in this hands-on yet strategic role you will have the following capabilities:
  • Excellent leadership and communication skills.
  • Proven experience in managing agricultural operations.
  • Strong knowledge of agricultural production, sustainability practices, and business processes.
  • Appreciation of natural capital.
  • Ideally experience working in a corporate environment.
  • Tertiary qualifications in Agriculture or Business Management preferred
  
Being a self-starter, you are motivated with the ability to work towards deadlines. With a strong team orientation, you are willing to work with others to achieve results.

Why This Role

This portfolio is an exciting role as the business is establishing its core DNA and culture and open to a leader to put your stamp on the business and take it to the next level. You might be a well experienced GM or have experience managing a couple of Farm Managers and ready to step up to GM.

Whilst Tamworth would be an ideal base for this role, there is flexibility to be located anywhere along the eastern seaboard, provided there is convenient access to a well-connected airport.

How to Apply: 
For a confidential discussion, contact AL Kellaway on 1300 380 701. Applications via www.rimfireresources.com.au.

job.title: Chief Executive Officer
job.description:
The Company
As Australia’s trusted leader in rice breeding, Rice Breeding Australia (RBA) delivers high performing varieties designed for the future of farming.

The organisation exists to drive sustainable, profitable and resilient rice production by supporting farmers through innovation, adaptation and future-focused agricultural research. It operates collaboratively across the industry to efficiently develop high-quality rice varieties tailored to local farming needs.

A not-for-profit agricultural research organisation, RBA was established in 2022 as an industry joint venture between AgriFutures Australia, Ricegrowers’ Association of Australia and SunRice Group.

A key driver of RBA’s creation was recognition that future water scarcity will negatively impact Australian rice production, requiring transformative change to deliver urgent water productivity gains the industry needs.
  
The Position
Reporting to and working closely with the Board, the Chief Executive Officer is responsible for the overall strategy and management of Rice Breeding Australia Ltd.

The role is required to provide strong and clear leadership to RBA and its people internally and to RBA’s stakeholders externally. This includes strategy development and implementation; oversight of corporate governance, compliance, financial and human resources management; and directing communications, industry and stakeholder engagement.

As CEO, you will play a key role in continuing the transformation of the Australian rice industry towards a profitable and sustainable production system for the long-term, delivering urgent water productivity gains through innovation in plant genetics.
  
The Person
RBA is seeking to appoint an agri-business executive with the skills and experience to build momentum and continue to drive necessary industry outcomes.

With the progress that has been achieved since 2022, which has established the right people, processes and capacity to deliver on organisational objectives, the RBA Board is open to considering a part-time appointment and while Rice Breeding Australia is based in the Riverina, Southern NSW, candidate location is flexible but will require extended time on site in Leeton. 

We are keen to hear from you if you possess the following:
  • A background in Australian agribusiness, ideally including exposure to the rice industry, gained in an existing senior management position or as a strong next-step candidate
  • Experience in the oversight/leadership and strategic direction of an R&D focussed business or business unit
  • Ability to understand, relate to, and connect with important stakeholders in the agribusiness environment including growers, industry organisations, government, and the broader research community
  • Highly developed stakeholder engagement and communication skills with the ability to identify, build and maintain formal and informal networks
  • Understanding and experience of managing financial and non-financial risks
  • Ability to manage conflict and at times, deliver difficult messages with the ability to work autonomously, be outcome focussed, self-confident and resilient in nature
  • Strong business acumen with sound financial skills as well as an understanding of contemporary corporate governance
  • Ideally possess a basic understanding of the principles and practices of field crop variety breeding and commercialisation  
This opportunity will suit an experienced candidate who has experience at senior management level looking to make a real difference to industry or a candidate looking to step up in their career into their first CEO position. 

This is a rare opportunity to make a significant contribution to Australia’s rice industry and enhance the profitability and sustainability of Australian Rice Growers.

If you feel you have what it takes to deliver real value to industry, then please phone Mick Hay or Katrina Conlon on 1300 380 701 or apply via www.rimfireresources.com.au

job.title: Commodity Logistics Scheduler
job.description:
The Company

Riverina Oils is a leading Australian agribusiness and vertically integrated canola oil producer with a major crushing and refining facility in Wagga Wagga and a commercial head office in Melbourne. The business supplies high-quality Australian canola oil to domestic and export markets and produces premium meal for livestock and feed customers, with a reputation for strong grower relationships, quality and end-to-end supply chain capability.
  
The Opportunity

Reporting into the Logistics Manager, you will be responsible for the monitoring of stocks and scheduling freight movements to ensure production and distribution requirements are achieved.

Working closely with the onsite sourcing and production teams, you will liaise closely with a number of stakeholders, coordinating vehicle scheduling, production scheduling, load planning, and records management.
Responsibilities include:
  • Liaising with growers, bulk handlers and logistics partners throughout the supply chain
  • Accurate contract management including raising new tickets and confirming financial requirements
  • Ensure compliance with COR responsibilities and regularly update Freight Matrix
  • Maintain stocks at an adequate level and ensure ongoing accurate inventory oversight
  • Ensure despatch management is in line with the plant running capacity for seed intake and meal out loading
About You

To be successful in this role you will have experience working within a similar position or similar grains business and be looking to further develop your career within the sector. Tertiary qualifications in an agricultural or related field is desirable, however experience and knowledge within the grains sector will be beneficial.

You will have exceptional communication skills, both written and verbal, and enjoy working as part of a close knit, fast paced team environment. You will naturally be a problem solver and be able to multi-task with a high attention to detail.

In return you will be joining an industry leading business with continued growth plans who look to invest in their staff. This role is based at their Southbank Head office.

job.title: Packaging Technologist
job.description:
The Company
As a marketer, wholesaler and distributor of healthcare, medical, pharmaceutical, consumer products and animal care brands, EBOS Group Limited is large, diversified and market leading.

The Animal Care Division manufactures, markets and distributes a diverse range of branded companion animal care and veterinary products. Masterpet, part of the animal care division, is dedicated to enriching the lives of pets and the people who care for them. They have a portfolio of leading pet food, treats, health and care brands across Australia, New Zealand and International markets. Key Brands include Black Hawk and Vita pet.

With core values including obsessing about their customers, taking care of each other, doing what’s right, courageously speaking up and always searching for innovation; they are dedicated to providing quality products, services and education that people need for their pets to live long and healthy lives.

The Opportunity

A Packaging Technologist, is required to join the R&D and Innovation team to provide technical leadership, governance and expertise across the Masterpet packaging portfolio. Reporting to the Head of R&D and Innovation you will be ensuring packaging solutions support product quality, food safety, manufacturing performance, sustainability objectives, supply continuity and business growth.

This includes developing, implementing and continuous improvement of packaging systems across new product development, existing product optimisation and future capability programs.

Your responsibilities in this broad role include:
  • Working closely with R&D, procurement, manufacturing, quality, regulatory, marketing and external packaging partners
  • Providing independent technical expertise and ownership of the packaging requirements across the business
  • Lead the evaluation and development of packaging technologies
  • Acting as an internal subject matter expert, providing technical leadership
  • Identifying opportunities for innovation, cost optimisation, sustainability improvements and supply chain resilience
About You

To be successful in this role you will have:
  • Packaging experience across development, technology and commercialisation within FMCG, food, beverage, consumer goods or related industries.
  • Good communication and stakeholder engagement skills with ability to negotiate and influence
  • Experience leading packaging projects from conception to commercialisation
  • Relevant tertiary qualifications (Bachelor, Master or PhD) in disciplines such as packaging technology, chemical/food engineering, industrial design or materials science.
There is some domestic (regional NSW & QLD) travel in the role.

Why This Role

You may currently be in a similar Packaging Technologist role in either food, FMCG, animal health/ nutrition or pharmaceutical industries, however, are up for more of a challenge, perhaps with more variety. Come and be the key packaging member of the team bringing your expertise. Join a diverse business at an exciting time which is growing, providing career progression scope. Sydney is the head office (Eveleigh) where there is a hybrid WFH arrangement.
A generous salary package is on offer.

To find out more confidentially, and for a copy of the Position Description, please call Al Kellaway on 1300 380 701 or apply to rimfireresources.com.au.

job.title: Manager National Variety Trial (NVT) - Operations, Partnerships, & Strategy
job.description:
The Company

Grains Research and Development Corporation (GRDC) is responsible for planning, investing, and overseeing research, development, and extension for the grains sector in Australia. They meet the evolving needs of grain growers with a vision to be regarded as the grower’s “RD&E department.” GRDC believes it should be a valued grower asset that is open, transparent, and trusted - a true partner who seeks to be agile and business like in their operations and improve productivity and profitability for growers.

The Opportunity

GRDC is seeking a Manager - National Variety Trial – Operations, Partnerships, & Strategy, a key role supporting the world renowned NVT program.  

The National Variety Trials (NVT) program is one of GRDC’s highest profile projects. Established in 2005 it is solely managed and funded by GRDC on behalf of Australian grain growers. Since inception, the NVT program has expanded to become the largest coordinated variety trial network in the world with 9 out of 10 Australian grain growers using NVT information. The program assists Australian grain growers and their advisors in varietal decision making by providing information on commercially available grain varieties, including comparisons of yield performance, disease resistance and grain quality.

An exceptional opportunity to work in a collaborative and passionate team by working closely across GRDC and externally to help shape the NVT program. You will be responsible for the ongoing success and evolution of the NVT by overseeing several key national components of the program as listed in the PD.

The team has a flexible mindset, and your specific responsibilities will be dependent on your expertise, experience, and interests you bring to the GRDC. The successful candidate will work within the NVT national team alongside 3 established and experienced managers delivering a wide range of responsibilities.
  • NVT systems management: responsible for all aspects of NVT's Systems
  • NVT collaborative partnerships management: responsible for administration of all elements of NVT partnerships to increase the benefit the NVT delivers for the Australian grains industry
  • NVT strategy and innovation management: responsible for NVT strategy and innovation for the continuous improvement of the program
  • NVT breeder operations management: responsible for managing all aspects of NVT’s breeder focussed operations
